To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neural imaging pipelines are capable of jointly optimizing image development and content authenticity, and that this approach can be used to improve image manipulation detection accuracy by up to 50% when applied to a complex image distribution channel.

(1) neural imaging pipelines can replace camera internals, (2) neural imaging pipelines are jointly optimized for high fidelity photo development and reliable forensic photo analysis, (3) the proposed approach increases photo manipulation detection accuracy from ~45% to over ~90%.
neural networks can be trained to jointly optimize the fidelity of photo development and the reliability of provenance analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: Given a digital camera and a set of digital photographs, we would like to train a neural imaging pipeline to develop photographs from camera raw files in a way that maximizes their authenticity.
the problem of content authentication of images in complex distribution channels.
the following question: Can we design a camera that is provably better at leaving forensic evidence than a regular camera?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown how the entire image acquisition process can be jointly optimized with the end goal of reliable forensic analysis at its end.
the proposed neural imaging pipeline can be trained to produce a high-quality image with reliable provenance information.
the proposed approach can be used to improve the reliability of digital forensic analysis of images by optimizing the entire imaging pipeline for high-fidelity development and provenance analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can use deep learning for image manipulation detection and provenance analysis, and the proposed approach is more reliable than the traditional method.
we can build a camera that is more robust to manipulation.
the proposed method can be used for the development of more reliable imaging pipelines, which are capable of providing reliable provenance analysis for the end users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to design imaging pipelines that are both optimized for image quality and for reliable provenance analysis.
it is possible to jointly optimize for image fidelity and provenance analysis accuracy, and that the optimization is not limited by the choice of a particular provenance analysis algorithm.
the provenance of a photo is a function of the entire imaging pipeline, and can be optimized for reliability in the distribution channel.
